sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Cape Coral?
sections.html:
Cape Coral sits in Lee County, so the Lee County Tax Collector mails and collects your bill, while the Lee County Property Appraiser sets the value and handles exemptions. The city only sets its own millage rate and its special assessments.

That split explains most phone calls. Questions about your value, mailing address or exemptions go to the property appraiser at 239-533-6100. Questions about paying, receipts and refunds go to the tax collector. Questions about a specific levy on the bill go to the authority named on the bill.

Census QuickFacts counts 236,264 residents in Cape Coral as of July 1, 2025, up 21.8% from the April 2020 base. The city covers 106.02 square miles of land, and 77.2% of housing units are owner-occupied. Median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $373,500, and 25.0% of residents are 65 or older.

The same Census table lists 82,914 households at 2.59 persons each, median gross rent of $1,858 and a mean commute of 29.9 minutes. For a seller, those figures describe a market of long-term owners: 88.2% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: What does the City of Cape Coral charge on top of the county?
sections.html:
The city levies an operating millage rate, and its own news release says council kept that rate at 5.1471 mills in the Fiscal Year 2027 budget approved at the September 24 hearing. A mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of taxable value, and the city rate is only one line among several taxing authorities on your bill.

The same release says the budget keeps the Fire Service Assessment at 81 percent. Special assessments such as fire and solid waste appear on the tax bill as non-ad valorem charges, which are flat amounts that do not depend on your home's value.

  • Ad valorem lines: city, county, school board and special districts, each with its own millage.
  • Non-ad valorem lines: city fire and solid waste assessments and similar service charges.
  • Your parcel's exact figures: the city's Property Checkbook tool lists the city tax, assessments and fees for an address.

sections.h2: What is Amendment 3 and does it change a Cape Coral bill I owe?
sections.html:
Per the Lee County Tax Collector, Amendment 3 passed and takes effect January 1, 2027, so it does not alter a 2026 bill, which is due by March 31, 2027.

The city's own toolkit page describes the proposal's local effect: 91.4% of the city is residential and 60.8% of improved residential properties are homesteaded. The city estimates a $31.1 million revenue loss in year one and $56.9 million in year two, citing the Florida Office of Economic and Demographic Research. Those are the city's projections, not figures on your bill.

If you plan to sell, the practical point is that the bill you owe at closing follows the rules and millage of the tax year it covers. Ask the tax collector or your closing agent which year's bill applies to your closing date.

sections.h2: What are the Lee County tax dates a Cape Coral owner should know?
sections.html:
The appraiser values property as of January 1, exemption applications are due March 1, and the tax collector mails bills in November, due by March 31 of the next year.

Lee County property tax calendar as printed by the appraiser and tax collector
WhenWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment for all properties
March 1Filing deadline for all exemptions and agricultural classification
July 1Appraiser submits the assessment roll to the Department of Revenue
AugustTRIM notices mailed; 25 days from mailing to petition the Value Adjustment Board
NovemberBills mailed; 4% discount if paid in November
December, January, FebruaryDiscounts of 3%, 2% and 1%
March 31Bill due in full
April 1Unpaid taxes delinquent

Applications filed after March 1 may be granted for the following year, according to the appraiser's calendar.

sections.h2: Can I pay a Cape Coral property tax bill in installments?
sections.html:
Yes, Lee County offers an installment plan, a partial payment plan and a homestead deferral, each with its own deadline.

For the installment plan, you apply between November 1 and April 30 of the tax year, the estimated tax must be above $100 per notice, and the schedule runs June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31. The first payment carries a 6% discount, the second 4.5%, the third 3% and the fourth none. The tax collector states that the 2026 installment window closed April 30, 2026, so the next application period covers 2027 taxes.

  • Partial payments: current year taxes only, up to five payments per account, no discounts, not accepted online, and delinquent taxes are not eligible.
  • Homestead deferral: apply by March 31; deferred taxes become a lien and fire insurance with a loss payable clause is required.
  • If a property sells after installments begin, the new owner continues the plan for that year.

sections.h2: How do Cape Coral homeowners get homestead and appeal a value?
sections.html:
File with the Lee County Property Appraiser by March 1, with the home as your permanent residence on January 1. The state exemption is up to $50,000: the first $25,000 applies to all taxes, and the added $25,000 applies to value over $50,000 for non-school taxes.

After the first homestead year, the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1, which is why a buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours. Portability lets you carry savings to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years of January 1 of the year you gave up the old one.

To challenge value, use the TRIM notice mailed in August. The appraiser's calendar gives 25 days from the mailing date to file with the Value Adjustment Board, and informal conferences with the appraiser can be requested at any time during the year.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when you sell a Cape Coral house?
sections.html:
The closing agent charges and credits each side for its share of the year, and the full-year bill goes to the owner of record, per the tax collector's FAQ.

If the bill arrives after you sold, forward it to the new owner or your closing agent; the collector explains that ownership changes reach the appraiser through the clerk, so timing can lag. Unpaid prior-year tax is delinquent after April 1 and is paid off from proceeds like any other lien. Delinquent taxes cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck.

Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in most counties, and all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay. Ask your title company for the exact taxes, assessments and prorations on your closing statement.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Cape Coral property tax value?
faqs.a: Call the Lee County Property Appraiser at 239-533-6100 for value, exemptions and mailing address changes. The tax collector handles payments and receipts at 239-533-6000.

faqs.q: Is Cape Coral's city millage rate 5.1471?
faqs.a: The city's news release says council approved the Fiscal Year 2027 budget on September 24 while maintaining the operating millage rate at 5.1471. Your total bill adds county, school and other authorities, so check your parcel on the tax collector's site.

faqs.q: When are Lee County taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: Taxes are delinquent after the March 31 due date, starting April 1. The tax collector's pages say delinquent real estate taxes cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck.

faqs.q: Does the installment plan transfer when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax collector says a new owner must continue the plan for that tax year if installments were already paid. Confirm the balance with the closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cape Coral house with unpaid tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid taxes are settled at closing from the sale proceeds. Request a payoff figure from the Lee County Tax Collector and have the title company include it.
